title: Verdier exchange from absolute trace adjunctions and a projection formula
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y$ be locally small symmetric monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category], with tensor symmetry $\sigma_{V,W}:V\otimes W\xrightarrow{\sim}W\otimes V$ (natural, involutive, and satisfying the hexagon with the associators). Let $\mathcal S$ be a locally small category and $\Omega\in\mathcal S$. Suppose given functors $P_T:\mathcal C_T\to\mathcal S$, $A_T:\mathcal S\to\mathcal C_T$ and adjunctions $P_T\dashv A_T$ for $T=X,Y$. An adjunction means specified Hom bijections natural in both variables; denote its counit at $\Omega$ by $\operatorname{tr}_T:P_T\omega_T\to\Omega$, where $\omega_T=A_T\Omega$. Suppose that, for every $M\in\mathcal C_T$, the internal Hom into $\omega_T$ exists: it is a contravariant functor $D_T:\mathcal C_T^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C_T$ equipped with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_{T,M}:D_TM\otimes M\to\omega_T$ such that $v\mapsto\operatorname{ev}_{T,M}\circ(v\otimes1_M)$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(W,D_TM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(W\otimes M,\omega_T)$ natural in $W,M$.

Let $F:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$ and $U:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$ be functors, with a right adjoint $R$ to $U$ and ordinary counit $\varepsilon:UR\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C_X}$. Suppose given natural isomorphisms
$$\kappa:P_YF\xrightarrow{\sim}P_X,\qquad \theta_{M,W}:FM\otimes W\xrightarrow{\sim}F(M\otimes UW).$$
Define $\tau:F\omega_X\to\omega_Y$ to be the transpose, under $P_Y\dashv A_Y$, of $\operatorname{tr}_X\circ\kappa_{\omega_X}:P_YF\omega_X\to\Omega$. For $M\in\mathcal C_X$ put $J_M=RD_XM$ and define $E_M:J_M\to D_YFM$ to be the tensor-Hom transpose of
$$\lambda_M=\tau\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_{X,M}\circ\sigma_{M,D_XM})\circ F(1_M\otimes\varepsilon_{D_XM})\circ\theta_{M,J_M}\circ\sigma_{J_M,FM}:J_M\otimes FM\to\omega_Y.$$
Then $E_M$ is an isomorphism natural contravariantly in $M$. More precisely, the inverse of the following natural composite bijection is postcomposition by $E_M$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Y(W,D_YFM)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(W\otimes FM,\omega_Y)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal S}(P_Y(W\otimes FM),\Omega)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal S}(P_X(M\otimes UW),\Omega)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(M\otimes UW,\omega_X)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(UW,D_XM)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(W,RD_XM).
\end{aligned}$$
The middle bijection uses $P_Y(\theta_{M,W}\circ\sigma_{W,FM})$ followed by $\kappa_{M\otimes UW}$, and the fifth uses tensor symmetry and the specified evaluation bijection. No relative right adjoint of $F$, biduality, or coefficient-change datum is assumed.

proof.text: Write $\Phi_{M,W}$ for the displayed composite in the statement. First spell out the adjunction conventions. If $L\dashv B$ has Hom bijection $\alpha$, its counit at $Z$ is $t_Z=\alpha^{-1}(1_{BZ})$; naturality in the source gives $\alpha^{-1}(v)=t_Z\circ L(v)$ for every $v:H\to BZ$. Thus the inverse of the $U\dashv R$ bijection sends $h:W\to RD_XM$ to $g_h=\varepsilon_{D_XM}\circ U(h)$. The $P_T\dashv A_T$ bijection sends $v:H\to\omega_T$ to $\operatorname{tr}_T\circ P_T(v)$. In particular, the definition of $\tau$ gives the exact equality $\operatorname{tr}_Y\circ P_Y(\tau)=\operatorname{tr}_X\circ\kappa_{\omega_X}$. These formulas follow by applying naturality to the identity defining each counit; no triangle identity beyond the stipulated Hom adjunction is needed.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1, displayed Hom bijections: agent-explicit categorical exchange lemma supplying the formal-exchange arrow without an ambient admissibility hypothesis.

proof.text: For $h:W\to J_M$ put $e_M^r=\operatorname{ev}_{X,M}\circ\sigma_{M,D_XM}$, $b_h=e_M^r\circ(1_M\otimes g_h):M\otimes UW\to\omega_X$, and $q_{M,W}=\kappa_{M\otimes UW}\circ P_Y(\theta_{M,W}\circ\sigma_{W,FM})$. Reverse the displayed chain, starting with $h$. The successive morphisms are $g_h$, then $b_h$, then $\operatorname{tr}_X\circ P_X(b_h)$, then $\operatorname{tr}_X\circ P_X(b_h)\circ q_{M,W}$, then its $P_Y\dashv A_Y$ transpose $c_h:W\otimes FM\to\omega_Y$, and finally the tensor-Hom transpose of $c_h$. Every operation is bijective: the Hom adjunctions are hypotheses, tensor symmetry and $q$ are isomorphisms, and the internal-Hom bijections are hypotheses. Hence these operations define $\Psi_{M,W}=\Phi_{M,W}^{-1}$, natural in $W$ by the assumed naturality of each operation. The tensor bifunctor and composition conventions are those of [def-sfb-monoidal-category].

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1, displayed Hom bijections: agent-explicit categorical exchange lemma supplying the formal-exchange arrow without an ambient admissibility hypothesis.

proof.text:
Compute the intermediate $P_Y\dashv A_Y$ transpose explicitly. Set $d_h=F(b_h)\circ\theta_{M,W}\circ\sigma_{W,FM}$. Functoriality, naturality of $\kappa$ at $b_h$, and the trace equality in step 1 give
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{tr}_Y\circ P_Y(\tau\circ d_h)
&=\operatorname{tr}_X\circ\kappa_{\omega_X}\circ P_YF(b_h)\circ P_Y(\theta_{M,W}\circ\sigma_{W,FM})\\
&=\operatorname{tr}_X\circ P_X(b_h)\circ\kappa_{M\otimes UW}\circ P_Y(\theta_{M,W}\circ\sigma_{W,FM})\\
&=\operatorname{tr}_X\circ P_X(b_h)\circ q_{M,W}.
\end{aligned}$$
Injectivity of the stipulated adjunction bijection therefore gives $c_h=\tau\circ F(b_h)\circ\theta_{M,W}\circ\sigma_{W,FM}$. This identifies the actual transpose, rather than merely an abstract isomorphism of representing objects.

proof.text:
Naturality of $\theta$ in $W$, followed by naturality of tensor symmetry, says
$$\theta_{M,J_M}\circ\sigma_{J_M,FM}\circ(h\otimes1_{FM})=F(1_M\otimes U(h))\circ\theta_{M,W}\circ\sigma_{W,FM}.$$
Substitute $g_h=\varepsilon_{D_XM}\circ U(h)$ and $b_h=e_M^r\circ(1_M\otimes g_h)$ into step 3. The tensor bifunctor's composition law and functoriality of $F$ give
$$c_h=\tau\circ F(e_M^r)\circ F(1_M\otimes\varepsilon_{D_XM})\circ\theta_{M,J_M}\circ\sigma_{J_M,FM}\circ(h\otimes1_{FM})=\lambda_M\circ(h\otimes1_{FM}).$$
Only the tensor bifunctor laws from [def-sfb-monoidal-category] and the naturalities explicitly assumed in the item were used.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1, displayed Hom bijections: agent-explicit categorical exchange lemma supplying the formal-exchange arrow without an ambient admissibility hypothesis.

proof.text: By definition of $E_M$, $\operatorname{ev}_{Y,FM}\circ(E_M\otimes1_{FM})=\lambda_M$. Consequently $\operatorname{ev}_{Y,FM}\circ((E_M\circ h)\otimes1_{FM})=\lambda_M\circ(h\otimes1_{FM})=c_h$. Injectivity of the specified tensor-Hom bijection shows $\Psi_{M,W}(h)=E_M\circ h$. Thus the inverse of the displayed composite is precisely postcomposition with the map required in the statement, for every $W$ and every $h$.

proof.text: Check the variance in $M$ explicitly. For $a:M'\to M$ and $h:W\to RD_XM$, let $h'=R(D_Xa)\circ h$. Counit naturality gives $g_{h'}=D_Xa\circ g_h$. Naturality of the specified internal-Hom evaluation and symmetry gives $e_{M'}^r\circ(1_{M'}\otimes D_Xa)=e_M^r\circ(a\otimes1_{D_XM})$, so $b_{h'}=b_h\circ(a\otimes1_{UW})$. Apply naturality of $\theta$ in $M$ and of symmetry to the formula in step 3: it yields $c_{h'}=c_h\circ(1_W\otimes F(a))$. Naturality of the $Y$ internal-Hom bijection now gives $\Psi_{M',W}(h')=D_Y(F(a))\circ\Psi_{M,W}(h)$. Taking $W=J_M$ and $h=1_{J_M}$ in step 5 proves $E_{M'}\circ R(D_Xa)=D_Y(F(a))\circ E_M$, the claimed contravariant naturality.

proof.text: For fixed $M$, step 5 is a natural isomorphism of representable presheaves $h_{J_M}\to h_{D_YFM}$, since $\Psi$ is a natural bijection by step 2. Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in the locally small category $\mathcal C_Y$. Its bijection identifies this transformation with $E_M$ (evaluate at $1_{J_M}$), and identifies its inverse with a morphism $H_M:D_YFM\to J_M$. Under the same bijection composition is postcomposition of morphisms, so the two inverse transformation identities give $H_M\circ E_M=1_{J_M}$ and $E_M\circ H_M=1_{D_YFM}$. Thus $E_M$ is an isomorphism; step 6 supplies its naturality and step 5 supplies the more precise clause.

With F=Rf_!, U=f^*, R=Rf_*, P=Ra_!, A=Ra^!, kappa the compact-support composition and theta the projection formula, E_M is exactly the exchange Rf_*D_XM -> D_Y Rf_!M. The citer lem-coef-finite-exceptional applies the item with exactly these substitutions and uses only invertibility and the Hom action, which the statement gives. I recomputed all seven steps. (1) The counit formula gives g_h=eps∘U(h) and tr_Y∘P_Y(tau)=tr_X∘kappa. (2) The middle bijection's inverse is precomposition with q; the types check, and b_h matches the inverse of 'symmetry then evaluation' by naturality of sigma. (3) Naturality of kappa at b_h gives c_h. (4) Naturality of theta in W and of sigma gives c_h=lambda_M∘(h⊗1). (5) So Psi(h)=E_M∘h. (6) Contravariant naturality holds; the evaluation identity ev_{M'}(D_X a⊗1)=ev_M(1⊗a) follows from the assumed naturality in M at v=1. (7) The Yoneda leaf lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful (Stacks 001P, categories.tex lemma-yoneda) gives the inverse and is used for what its statement says. Small cases: with identity data E=id; in vector spaces with scalars c,d for theta,kappa, E=cd·id; with a zero dualizing object the claim holds trivially.
